chapter: Virginia school and first Washington bands
title: Tommy Miles band personnel
summary: He names the pianist Garnett Clark, the size of the band and its saxophones, trombones, trumpets and rhythm section.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: And we had a piano player named Garnett Clark, fantastic little young piano player. He went to Europe years ago. He died in Paris. He was a kind of wild guy. He played with Charlie Barnett for a while way back there then. You know, Charlie was integrated long before anybody else, you know. He went with Charlie -- he went with him way back there then. And there was -- he was amazing piano player. He was a
How many -- how big a band did Tommy Miles have?
Oh, we had two trombones, we had three trumpets -- that's five -- we had four saxophones -- that's nine -- we had guitar, piano, drums and bass. About 13, 14 pieces.
Do you remember who all else was in the band besides the ones you've mentioned?

That would -- one of the guys his name was Wash Washington. He's a dentist now. He was going to dental school up at Howard University. And he was playing with us. He was an alto player. We had another alto player named Johnny Harris. And Jimmy Munday was the tenor player. And we had another saxophone player, I can't recall now.

And Tommy Miles was the drummer. Garnett Clark was the piano player. I think Chester -- what was Chester's last name -- was a guitar player, because there's another guitar player with the other band, with Booker Coleman, that was Jimmy Owens. He's a fantastic guitar player. He played violin. He died early. And the bass player was Bass Hill, we called him, Pop Hill. He played around New York for a long time. He was on that band on bass.

And the trombones was myself, and another guy named Wendell Jackson from Richmond, Virginia. And the trumpet

players were Warner Carter, Warren Jefferson, and I just can't recall the other trumpet player. But Warren Jefferson went with Earl Hines when I went him, and played lead trumpet with Earl. And he was with Earl, and he didn't stay a real, real long time but he was a good musician. He could range and he could read real well. We had some very good musicians as far as reading and arranging on that band.
